research_updates.title: County parcel resolves CL4's building-level fiscal history
research_updates.notes: Mecklenburg County identifies parcel 14106108 at 1805 Center Park Drive as a 1999 computer data center. Annual real-property bills from 2013 through 2026 provide assessed value, county and city levies, total billed and verified payments. TierPoint's CL4 page identifies the same address, but TierPoint is the tenant and the building predates the 2014 CL4 opening; the series therefore documents parcel fiscal contribution without attributing every change to TierPoint.

source.title: Mecklenburg County property record — 1805 Center Park Drive parcel 14106108
source.notes: The official property record identifies parcel 14106108 at 1805 Center Park Drive, classifies the 1999 building as a COMPUTER DATA CENTER, reports 60,246 square feet of finished area, names Gannett DC Assets LP as the current owner, and links the parcel's annual tax bills. TierPoint's current CL4 page identifies the same address, but TierPoint is the building tenant rather than the real-property taxpayer.

research_updates.title: Investment audit and project boundary
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: operator and predecessor releases; developer records; landlord valuation/property materials; SEC filings; assessor and transaction references; local reporting and archives. Exact queries/entities/identifiers: TierPoint CL4, Charlotte Four, Windstream Hosted Solutions, Server Farm Realty, SFR NC1 LLC, DSA Encore, 1805 Center Park Drive, parcel/APN 14106108/141-061-08 and Mecklenburg Registry Book 28412 Page 204, covering 2012-2026. Material records opened: June 26, 2013 groundbreaking release, March 3, 2014 opening release, Mapletree valuation, SEC lease schedule and Windstream 10-K. Useful result: exact boundary, opening facts and operator succession. The planned 60,850 square feet/10 MW, a secondary $15 million 'expansion' assertion, real-estate appraisals/sales and the $575 million portfolio acquisition cannot establish CL4 productive investment; investment remains a gap rather than a proxy.

source.title: Windstream opens fourth-generation data center in Charlotte, N.C.
source.notes: Contemporaneous opening release reports 39,300 total square feet, 10,380 square feet of raised floor, 3,000 kVA first-day utility capacity, 1,215 kW of usable first-day UPS capacity, 530 tons of first-day cooling and an onsite network operations center fully staffed 24 x 7 x 365. Whole-building, raised-floor and UPS observations are encoded separately. Utility kVA and cooling tons lack matching governed direct-evidence metrics and remain structured source facts; the NOC statement anchors a minimum one-post staffing-equivalent sensitivity, not an observed employee count. The release's 60,800 total square feet, more than 20,500 square feet of raised floor, more than 12 MVA utility, more than 3,600 kW UPS and 1,350 tons cooling are phased expansion capabilities, not opening-day facts. It provides no investment, headcount, payroll, residence or measured resource-use total.

research_updates.title: Construction audit
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Charlotte/Mecklenburg planning, zoning, building, mechanical, plumbing, electrical, generator, grading, land-disturbance and stormwater records in Accela and legacy WebPermit. Exact searches: address 1805 CENTER PARK, parcel 14106108, TierPoint, Windstream, Server Farm, SFR NC, Gannett, project names CL4/PMC Expansion and 2012-2026. Material records opened: address object 368923; projects 419519, 435613, 438007 and 469431; B3960984 and linked subpermits; Accela COM-ALT-25-000615 and COM-ALT-26-000979. Useful result: finaled 2021 renovation with $2,580,200 administrative contract cost. No exact 2013 conversion permit returned; $297,000 and $370,600 expired records, the $425,000 non-finaled 2025 project, $14.399 million in-progress 2026 PMC expansion and withdrawn Phase 2 are excluded. Negative portal results cannot prove no historic permit.

source.title: Building permit B3960984, TierPoint CL4 Renovations
source.notes: Official permit for project 419519 identifies a 15,008-square-foot upfit/interior renovation at the exact address, owner/tenant Gannett, contractor Duffey Southeast, and $2,580,200 total contract cost across the master and linked subpermits. All four linked permits were finaled. The value is an administrative permit amount, not audited spending, payroll, local procurement or an opening-phase cost; displayed permit fees were not verified as paid and are excluded.

research_updates.title: Supplier audit
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: developer/contractor materials, permit contractor fields, county procurement/vendor access points, subcontractor/supplier references and local reporting; exact queries TierPoint Charlotte, CL4, Windstream Charlotte Four, SFR NC1, DSA Encore, Duffey Southeast, 1805 Center Park and permit/project identifiers for 2012-2026. Material records identify Server Farm Realty and DSA Encore for the planned build-to-suit and Duffey Southeast for the 2021 renovation. No paid contract, subcontractor list, supplier invoice, procurement award, local-business classification, local-spend amount or contractor payroll was published. Named firms establish participation only; no supplier contribution amount is created.

source.title: TierPoint Charlotte data-technology portfolio
source.notes: Contractor case study corroborates work involving chillers, switchgear, a generator, partitions and 6,336 square feet of raised flooring. It publishes no contract payment, worker count, payroll, employee residence, subcontractor amount or local-supplier share.

research_updates.title: Operations audit
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: current/predecessor operator pages, opening materials, careers, workforce, occupation, residence, training, apprenticeship, County Business Patterns and federal/state filings; exact queries TierPoint CL4/Charlotte Center Park, Windstream Charlotte Four, 1805 Center Park, NOC, security, employee, jobs, payroll, technician and Charlotte over 2012-2026. The opening release says the onsite NOC was fully staffed 24 x 7 x 365, and the current CL4 page separately states 24x7 onsite security personnel; neither gives simultaneous posts, filled headcount, employer or payroll. Corrective synthesis evaluates each function independently as one-post staffing capacity: 8,760 hours / 2,080 paid hours per FTE x relief factor 1.00/1.15/1.30 = 4.21/4.84/5.48 FTE. The two sensitivities are not summed because role overlap and security contracting are unresolved, and neither is reported as observed employment. County NAICS 518210 establishments, March employment and payroll are 36 county-context rows from twelve CBP files, not CL4 inputs. Builder operations coverage therefore remains only 'partial' from physical/county context and must not be read as a complete project employment or payroll account.

source.title: TierPoint careers
source.notes: Careers materials describe data-center operations roles and company-wide VolunTiers/Gives Back activity. They do not disclose CL4 filled headcount, annual-average FTE, occupation mix, pay, payroll, employee residence, training or apprenticeship totals, nor a Charlotte recipient and transfer amount.

research_updates.title: Fiscal audit
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Mecklenburg assessor/property, annual tax bills and payments, personal-property, exemption and treasurer records; exact identifiers 1805 Center Park Drive, parcel 14106108/141-061-08, Gannett DC Assets LP, SFR NC1 LLC, Windstream and TierPoint, tax years 2013-2026. Material records: county property profile and each annual bill/payment already present in the base evidence, plus permit property links. Useful result: an exact real-property series through 2026. The parcel owner/taxpayer is Gannett DC Assets LP and TierPoint is the tenant; no crosswalked TierPoint/Gannett personal-property account, exemption schedule or tenant tax reimbursement was found. Real-property bills cover multiple taxing jurisdictions and are gross payments, not Charlotte-only revenue, taxpayer incidence or net fiscal benefit.

source.title: WebPermit address record for 1805 Center Park Drive
source.notes: Legacy address record links parcel 14106108 and seven projects, including 419519, 435613, 438007, 469431 and two nonresidential plan-review records. Project 435613's $297,000 electrical permit expired; project 438007's $370,600 upfit expired; project 469431's $425,000 generator/D-bus expansion was issued in 2025 but not finaled. They are excluded rather than treated as realized construction.

research_updates.title: Public-cost audit
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Charlotte and Mecklenburg development/incentive records, abatement, PILOT, bond, TIF, IRB, grant, compliance, audit, budget, ACFR, agendas, minutes, attachments, procurement and check-register sources, plus NCDOR/Commerce and NC statutory materials. Exact entity/address/parcel/project queries covered 2012-2026. No CL4-specific award, certified-data-center record, tax-expenditure amount, grant, financing, public infrastructure payment, compliance report, check, marginal police/fire/road/utility cost or net-benefit analysis was located. A Baltimore vendor dataset mentioning TierPoint Maryland was verified as the wrong jurisdiction and rejected. General North Carolina data-center tax law is eligibility context, not proof of CL4 receipt; public costs remain unknown, not zero.

source.title: Mecklenburg County Finance and Procurement
source.notes: County budget, ACFR, procurement and vendor-payment access points were searched using project names, entities, address and parcel for 2012-2026. No project-specific check-register payment, contract, public-service cost, infrastructure reimbursement or net fiscal analysis was found. A similarly named ArcGIS open-checkbook result was verified as Baltimore, not Charlotte, and rejected as wrong-jurisdiction evidence.

research_updates.title: Resource audit
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Duke electric-service references in permits; NCUC electric/gas tariff, docket, interconnection, transmission and substation records; Charlotte Water, wastewater, reclaimed-water and public-infrastructure sources; operator specifications. Exact searches TierPoint, Windstream Hosted Solutions, CL4, 1805 Center Park, parcel 14106108 and 2012-2026. Direct opening facts are 1.215 MW usable UPS, 3,000 kVA utility service and 530 tons cooling; current/specification facts include conflicting four-versus-two 2.25 MW generators, minimum 48-hour runtime, 8,000 gallons fuel and two 3,000 kVA transformers. Corrective electricity synthesis uses min(1.215 MW x utilization x PUE, 3,000 kVA x power factor / 1,000) x 1,000 x 8,760 with utilization 25/50/75%, PUE 1.2/1.4/1.6 and power factor 0.8/0.9/1.0, producing 3.193/7.450/12.772 million kWh theoretical annual scenarios; the utility ceiling does not bind. It is not actual use or a true bound. Cooling candidate equation 530 refrigeration tons x 12,000 Btu/hour = 6.36 million Btu/hour thermal was rejected as an electricity model because COP, part-load, redundancy and hours are absent. Generator nameplates were rejected as annual-energy inputs because emergency runtime/load are absent. No meter, bill, gas, water, wastewater, discharge, PUE/WUE, CIAC or infrastructure allocation was found.

source.title: North Carolina Utilities Commission docket search
source.notes: Docket searches covering 2012-2026 used TierPoint, Windstream Hosted Solutions, 1805 Center Park, CL4 and parcel 14106108. No facility-specific electric, gas, tariff, interconnection, contribution-in-aid-of-construction, transmission, substation, bill or load record was found. Generic Duke Energy tariffs cannot be converted into CL4 consumption or public impact.

research_updates.title: Community audit
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: TierPoint Gives Back/VolunTiers materials, operator news, Foundation For The Carolinas and Charlotte-area recipient-side grant and sponsorship references, using TierPoint, Windstream, CL4, Center Park and the exact address for 2012-2026. Company materials establish only a company-wide volunteering/giving program. No Charlotte or CL4 recipient confirmation, grant list entry, cash amount, in-kind valuation, date, restricted purpose or recurring commitment was found. Absence from searchable public pages cannot establish zero giving; community contribution remains an explicit gap.

source.title: TierPoint Green Finance Framework
source.notes: Framework reports $360,000 donated since the company-wide TierPoint Gives Back program began in 2017 and describes quarterly application-based giving. It does not identify a Charlotte or CL4 recipient, amount, date, purpose or allocation, so the fleet-wide total is not assigned to this project.

research_updates.title: Corrective parcel, incentive, archive and transaction gap closure
research_updates.notes: Second pass reopened the assessor/tax trail, SEC lease and acquisition filings, Mapletree valuation/property materials, NCDOR and Commerce program pages, NC General Statutes, Charlotte and BOCC agenda/minute archives, finance/procurement access points and exact-phrase web archives. Queries repeated historical/current legal entities, address, parcel, registry book/page and project identifiers across 2012-2026. Results resolved landlord/operator and portfolio-versus-building boundaries but produced no personal-property account, realized incentive amount, development agreement, IRB/TIF/PILOT, project financing, completion-cost ledger or auditable original investment. Secondary reports of a $15 million expansion and $26.4 million property acquisition conflict in timing or measure and were excluded rather than upgraded through repetition.

source.title: Important notice: repeal of exemptions for electricity used at datacenters
source.notes: Notice documents the statewide certified-data-center sales-tax framework and repeal timing for the electricity exemption. Searches of NCDOR and Commerce materials for TierPoint, Windstream, SFR NC1, CL4 and the address found no project-specific certificate, qualifying investment, claim, refund, exemption value, audit or compliance result, so no public-cost amount is assigned.

research_updates.title: Corrective permit, environmental, utility and infrastructure gap closure
research_updates.notes: Second pass used both legacy and current permit systems, exact record IDs, contractor/entity variations, Mecklenburg Air Quality's live PLC database, NC DEQ's state tracker, NCUC dockets and Charlotte Water/public-infrastructure access points. Local-air queries '1805 Center Park Drive', 'TierPoint', 'Windstream' and 'Gannett' returned zero PLC records; NC DEQ explicitly excludes Mecklenburg local-air permits and may remove closed applications. No initial conversion permit, air authorization, generator-emissions record, stormwater/NPDES record, meter, utility agreement, tariff rider or funded public infrastructure was found. These limits prevent absence claims. A low-confidence UPS/service engineering sensitivity is retained only because it is decision-relevant scale context and explicitly labeled theoretical; cooling, generator operation, water, emissions and utility-cost synthesis remain ineligible.

source.title: Mecklenburg County Air Quality public records database
source.notes: Public PLC-record searches for exact phrases '1805 Center Park Drive', 'TierPoint', 'Windstream' and 'Gannett' each returned zero records on September 7, 2026. The database directs users to Air Quality staff or public-record requests when records are missing, so the result does not establish that no historical permit, applicability determination or emissions source exists.

research_updates.title: Corrective workforce, supplier, community and structured-data gap closure
research_updates.notes: Second pass searched operator careers and community pages, permit contractor fields, developer/contractor cases, procurement/vendor sources, recipient-side references, SEC filings and official 2012-2023 Census County Business Patterns bulk files. The Census API required a key, so each annual county ZIP row for state 37, county 119, NAICS 518210 was inspected; noise flags and NAICS-version breaks are retained. Source count is 36 total: 24 non-CBP substantive sources plus twelve annual CBP files. The 36 CBP records are assigned to the project only as a consistent host-county industry-context panel and cannot satisfy CL4 headcount, payroll, resident-employment or causal-outcome gaps. The sources still provide no observed CL4 employee/payroll/residence record, construction workforce, contractor/subcontractor payment, local spend, recipient-confirmed community transfer or operating revenue/cost.

source.title: 2023 County Business Patterns county file
source.notes: Official annual ZIP row for state 37, county 119 and NAICS 518210 reports establishments, March employment and annual payroll. Employment noise flag is G; payroll noise flag is G. Census API access required a key, so the published bulk ZIP was used and the exact row was inspected. The series describes the entire county industry, not CL4, and crosses 2012, 2017 and 2022 NAICS classification vintages.

research_updates.title: Independent candidate-by-candidate modeling and county-outcome decision
research_updates.notes: Model eligibility review after gap closure — Investment: rejected because sales, appraisals and portfolio prices are not productive project cost. Construction: rejected because one 2021 permit value cannot produce labor, timing or opening-phase spend. Suppliers: rejected for missing paid/local shares. Operations observed headcount/payroll: unresolved, but two low-confidence one-post coverage sensitivities are retained separately because facility-specific 24x7 NOC and onsite-security statements make the scheduling calculation decision-relevant; neither is observed employment and they are not summed. Fiscal: rejected beyond direct parcel bills/payments because tenant incidence and personal property are unresolved. Public costs: rejected for no award, expenditure or marginal service input. Resources actual use: unresolved, but one low-confidence UPS/service annual-energy sensitivity is retained as theoretical scale context; cooling, generators, water, emissions and cost models are rejected for missing operating inputs. Community: rejected for no recipient-confirmed amount. County employment and wages: rejected despite mechanical post-2014 gaps of 9.54% and 8.23% because multiple local facilities, a 2013 building conversion, later expansions, donor contamination and no CL4 workforce bridge defeat attribution. County GDP: rejected; the mechanical 53.11% gap had 55.55% pre-period RMSE and an interval spanning -57.98% to 164.20%. Descriptively, 2013-2024 Mecklenburg GDP, employment and nominal weekly wage rose 49.44%, 34.45% and 50.98%, respectively, without attribution. Modeled additions: three; all remain standalone, low-confidence, modeled-not-observed syntheses.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project. project_description: TierPoint Charlotte Center Park (CL4) is the TierPoint-operated colocation building at 1805 Center Park Drive in Charlotte, Mecklenburg County, North Carolina; it is distinct from TierPoint's Charlotte-North Myers facility and the wider Carolinas portfolio. Server Farm Realty and DSA Encore announced the build-to-suit project in June 2013, and Windstream Hosted Solutions officially opened it on March 3, 2014 with 39,300 square feet and 1.215 MW of usable UPS capacity, while describing larger figures only as phased expansion plans. TierPoint succeeded Windstream as operator after a 2015 portfolio acquisition, and 2020 landlord records describe the parcel as a 60,850-square-foot single-story property that was 66.7% leased to TierPoint. County permit records separately identify completed 2021 renovations and later expired, withdrawn or in-progress work, which this account does not treat as part of the opening phase.
